elements.texte:
[cheerful] The loyalty team is preparing the report on its points program.

The report must show every customer, even those who don’t have a loyalty card.

To prepare this report, we need to bring together the information from the customers and loyalty tables.

The points are in the loyalty table, but only 4 customers have a card.

So we need to combine the two tables to get the points, without leaving out the customers who have no card.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] First try: inner join links each customer to their loyalty card.

With inner join, only the 4 customers who have a card show up in the result.

The 6 customers with no card are left out of the result. So the report is incomplete.

We need a join that keeps every customer, even without a card.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] To also keep the customers with no card, replace inner join with left join.

The condition after ON stays the same.

The customers table, placed before left join, is the left table. All its rows are kept.

Sophie Martin, Lucas Bernard, Nathan Petit and Léa Simon get their card back thanks to ON.

The 6 other customers are kept anyway: 10 customers, 10 rows.
